title: Why children become unusually quiet after being scolded: Psychology explains
content: When kids are reprimanded, their quietness often reveals a mix of shame or embarrassment. They might worry about letting their parents down, leading them to suppress their feelings. Consistent criticism can teach them that staying silent feels safer than voicing their thoughts. Instead of further scolding during these moments, parents should provide empathy and support. It's crucial to reconnect with children after these instances to foster healthy emotional growth.
